example: Inputs: Last Menstrual Period 10 August 2026, Cycle Length 28 days. Step 1: add 280 days to 10 August 2026, which gives 17 May 2027. Step 2: the cycle is 28 days, so no adjustment is needed. Step 3: on 21 November 2026, days since LMP = 103 days, which is 14 weeks and 5 days. Final result: estimated due date 17 May 2027, currently in week 14 (2nd trimester), with 177 days remaining. This is an estimate, not a medical prediction.

faqs.a: It is an estimate based on a 280-day pregnancy from the last period. Real delivery dates commonly fall within about two weeks either side, and an early ultrasound gives a more accurate date.
faqs.q: How accurate is the due date from LMP?

faqs.a: Enter your usual cycle length. The calculator adds (cycle length − 28) days to the 280-day count, so a 32-day cycle moves the due date 4 days later.
faqs.q: What if my cycle is not 28 days?

faqs.a: Weeks 1–12 are the 1st trimester, weeks 13–26 the 2nd, and week 27 onwards the 3rd. The calculator shows your trimester with the result.
No. The result is an estimate for planning only. For any health question in pregnancy, consult a doctor.

formula: Estimated Due Date (EDD) = LMP date + 280 days + (cycle length − 28) days. Pregnancy week = whole days since LMP ÷ 7. Trimesters: weeks 1–12 first, 13–26 second, 27 and above third.
howTo: Enter the first day of your last menstrual period in the Last Menstrual Period (LMP) field.
Enter your usual cycle length in the Cycle Length (days) field, for example 28.
Tap Calculate to see the estimated due date.
Read the current week, day, and trimester shown under the result.
Use the days-remaining figure to plan check-ups and preparations.
intro: The Pregnancy Due Date Calculator estimates the expected delivery date from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP), and shows the current week and trimester.
mistakes: Entering the last day of the period instead of the first day, which shifts the due date by several days.
Leaving the cycle length at 28 when your usual cycle is longer or shorter.
Treating the estimated due date as a guaranteed delivery date.
Using the calculator instead of a doctor's dating scan when the dates do not match.
tips: The most accurate LMP is the first day of the last period, not the day it ended.
If your cycles are irregular, the estimate is less reliable — an ultrasound date from your doctor is more accurate.
Only about a small share of babies arrive exactly on the due date, so treat it as a guide week, not a fixed appointment.
Keep a note of the due date and share it with your doctor at the first visit.
This calculator is an estimate only. All health decisions in pregnancy should be made with a doctor.
uses: It is used to estimate a due date, work out how many weeks pregnant someone is, find the current trimester, and count the days remaining until the due date.
